# Sonar Picket Playbook

**HIDING**
When choosing where to hide, avoid the center cells (4-5-6) initially as they are common default choices. Rotate through different zones across rounds rather than staying in one area. After being hit, move away from that cell; after being missed, consider that the shooter may adjust. Track who fired at you and anticipate their next shot will adjust based on their miss pattern. When leading significantly late in the game, move to corner cells (1, 9) or edges (2, 8) to escape predictable center clustering—corners are psychologically less obvious than middle retreats.

**STATION NOTES**
Use notes sparingly and for genuine coordination, not empty signaling. Early cooperation talk wastes space and doesn't change behavior. Once a note like "steady on station" is established with other boats, maintain it consistently across rounds—consistency itself signals stability and reduces uncertainty. Keep notes minimal and factual. Don't try to manipulate through notes; use them only when you have real tactical information to share.

**FIRING**
Fire at your standing order target. Vary your fire cell rather than repeating the same number—I fired 5 multiple times early in the game and this became predictable to my target. When you have a lead late in the game, understand your standing order target may adjust their hiding based on your pattern, so vary cells across the board rather than clustering around the middle. In the final rounds, fire at cells your target is likely to retreat to after you've established a pattern of center-firing, not at the center itself.

**CLAIMS**
When the office tells you the true result of your shot, file that result honestly. Do not lie on your claim even in the final round. The office knows the truth and validates it. False claims damage your credibility and may trigger official penalties. Your score matters more than a single round's deception. Honesty builds trust and enables better coordination with other boats.

**ESCORT CLAIMS**
Track which boats might escort you and which you might escort back for mutual 5-point gains. Don't claim escort with boats unless you have actual coordination and can verify it happened. When you don't know if an escort happened, say none rather than guessing. Late in the game when leading, securing mutual escorts is a lower priority than avoiding being hit—focus on survival over incremental gains.

**OVERALL STRATEGY**
Build and maintain a reputation for honesty on shot claims. This matters because deception creates instability and reduces the benefit of any coordination. Protect your lead by hiding unpredictably once you're ahead—move to corners and edges, not just center adjustments. Don't rely on center cells. Vary everything: hide cells, fire cells, and patterns. Acknowledge when a tactic fails and adjust immediately rather than repeating it. When you've established a consistent hiding pattern (like moving through zones), enemies will target based on that pattern, so break it in the final rounds by moving to extreme positions they won't predict.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding
When choosing a hiding position, vary between central positions (4-6) and edge positions (1-3, 7-9) unpredictably. Track which positions I've used and rotate away from them. If I notice a shooter has hit me twice in a row, move to a position I haven't used in recent rounds rather than trying to predict their next guess. In later rounds, if a shooter has missed me consistently (three or more times), they may be locked into a pattern—edge positions that break from my early central tendencies are worth exploring.

## Station Notes
Use my notes to signal stability and readiness. Keep notes consistent and bland—avoid sending information that reveals my strategy or position patterns to the table. "Steady on station" is reliable and has proven effective throughout the game.

## Firing
Always follow the standing order. I will fire at the designated target (in my case, Gamma). For cell selection, use position 5 (center) as a reliable opening, then vary based on observed patterns. Don't overthink cell selection in early rounds; fire positions should be spread to explore the line rather than clustered. If I land a hit early, continue rotating my firing cells to explore different parts of the line rather than staying clustered around a successful position.

## Claims
When the office tells me the true result of my shot, claim it truthfully every time. The claim must match the private result I receive. There is no value in lying about hits and misses.

## Escort Coordination
Track which boats might be willing to trade mutual escort claims for the 5-point payoff. When I claim to have escorted another boat, choose one that is likely to claim back. If I have no information about escort patterns, claim none rather than guess randomly. Mutual escort claims (5 points each) are worth more than a single shot (4 points), so establishing this coordination should be a priority for mid-game rounds.

## Overall Strategy
The payoff for hitting a target (4 points) is modest. The payoff for mutual escort claims (5 points each) exceeds a single shot. Invest mental effort in identifying which other boat might be willing to coordinate escort claims with me across multiple rounds. Don't waste rounds firing at Harbor—the threat is real and the payoff marginal. In this episode, I scored poorly (6 points) because I obtained one hit but never coordinated escort claims. Next game, establish escort coordination with one other boat by round 2 or 3, even if speculatively—the 5-point mutual payout compounds quickly and will outpace sporadic hits.

# Sonar Picket Checker Playbook

## Hiding

When choosing where to hide, avoid predictable patterns. Don't stay in the same cell round after round—rotate your position to make targeting harder. After observing which boats are firing at you consistently, move away from the cells where they've been hitting you. Central positions are reasonable for opening rounds, but vary them rather than anchoring to any single cell.

Track my own hiding history across the game. If I've used a cell recently, move away from it. If an opponent has hit me in a cell, strongly avoid returning there. If an opponent has missed repeatedly in a cell, they may be adapting, so don't assume safety.

## Station Notes

Post "steady on station" consistently. This is cooperative language that costs nothing and helps establish predictability in my own positioning, which I control. Don't overcomplicate my notes. Maintain this through the final round as part of the overall strategy of controlling what I can control.

## Firing

Follow the standing order without deviation. I have no discretion here—fire at my assigned target because that's the rule. Choose my fire cell based on pattern observation of where my target has been hiding recently. If I've hit a target before in a cell, they're likely to move away from it; if I've missed repeatedly in a cell, they may not be there. Look for recent rotation patterns in their hiding, not just individual cell history.

Against a target with strong recent behavior (like hitting me in cell 5), assume they will rotate to a neighboring or nearby alternative cell rather than moving randomly. This narrows the search space more effectively than scattering shots across the full line.

## Claims

Always file claims that match the private result the office gives me. This is mandatory and non-negotiable for game integrity. False claims corrupt my own decision-making in future rounds because I lose track of what's actually happening, and I cannot extract strategic value from a lie that only I know about. The office knows the truth; other players learn my patterns through observation. Lying to myself serves no one.

When the office tells me the true result of my shot, I match my claim to that result exactly. No exceptions, no matter what strategic intuition suggests.

## Escort Claims

When I name an escort, I need mutual recognition for the 5-point payoff. Name none unless I have a clear pre-established signal with another boat or have already observed mutual escort-naming in previous rounds. Don't guess. The penalty for an unreciprocated escort claim is silence—no points either way—so the risk-reward is asymmetric. Only name an escort when I have evidence of prior mutual intent.

## Overall Strategy

Pay close attention to which boats are targeting me and where they're hitting. Adjust my hiding accordingly. Observe which boats' hit and miss patterns indicate skill versus luck or random firing. Prioritize defensive positioning over all other considerations since I take 1 point per hit.

Track the standing order strictly and fire mechanically at my assigned target while varying fire cells based on observed opponent movement. Cooperate through consistent notes but compete through evasion and accurate shooting. The game rewards both reliable positioning information and hard-target defense; balance attention between understanding what others are doing and making myself hard to find.

In the final rounds, maintain all prior strategies—don't break discipline in round 6 just because points are running out. Consistency of approach compounds over time.
